paragraphs: Rabbi Oshaya the great. (1) Son of Chama bar Bisna: “The threefold cord” is Rabbi Oshaya bar Chama bar Bisna (see there). Tosafot, Chezkat Habattim 59a: Rabbi Oshaya is placed before his father Rabbi Chama in a dispute because he was exceptionally great, as in “The hearts of the earlier ones were like the entrance of the hall”—Rabbi Oshaya. He is called Berabbi, Yevamot 46b, 121b, where he disputed with eighty-five elders; Eruvin 53a; Chagigah 7a. Rashi: a great man in Torah (see Berabbi).

(2) He and Rabbi Chiyya (see there; the source’s parenthesis is malformed) made baraitot, Tosefta, and teachings. Every teaching not taught in Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Oshaya’s collections is corrupt; do not raise objections from it in the study hall. Rashi, Chullin 141, beginning of b: they arranged baraitot, taking care to state each sage’s precise words; many other reciters add to their teaching by analogy. Shabbat, first chapter: one baraita says ashes, another earth. Rashi: one was taught by Rabbi Chiyya, one by Rabbi Oshaya. This suggests every “it was taught” in the Talmud comes from these two. Bava Kamma: Rabbi Oshaya taught thirteen primary damages, Rabbi Chiyya twenty-four. Hagozel Kamma 94b, Rabbenu Tam: the mishnayot preceded Rabbi, who arranged them; the baraitot taught by his student Rabbi Chiyya are what Rabbi added to the mishnayot. This explains Rabbi Yose’s “Fortunate are you, Kelim, to have emerged in purity.” The Bereshit Rabbah he composed explains the Mishnah. (The Rokeach’s introduction says Bereshit Rabbah begins “I was delight,” whose numerical value is “Our master Hoshaya the great.” This is an error; I think it should read “This is Rabbi Oshaya the great.”) Tzemach David writes it is not the Bereshit Rabbah composed by Rabbah bar Nachmani. This requires examination: our Bereshit Rabbah begins “Rabbi Hoshaya the great opened: I was delight,” which accords with Rokeach’s view that he signed his name. Yet this Bereshit Rabbah explains no Mishnah, containing only Jerusalem-Talmud aggadot, and its author appears to have been Rabbah bar Nachmani. (See Rabbah, who composed Midrash Rabbah.) Raavad writes that Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Oshaya wrote Mekhilta (see Abba Arikha, Rabbi Yishmael, and Ben Azzai).

(3) He received from his father, bar Kappara, Rabbi Chiyya, and Rabbi’s court. Rabbi Hoshaya frequently attended bar Kappara, left him, and went to Rabbi Chiyya. One day they met, and he asked bar Kappara a question. Bar Kappara said, “What does the Babylonian”—Rabbi Chiyya—“say about this?” Rabbi Oshaya fell silent. Bar Kappara said, “We need Aiya’s words”—Chiyya, addressed disparagingly, Keritot 8a. His father and bar Kappara disagreed, etc. Does this not mean he heard from his father? No: he heard from his teacher bar Kappara, Mo'ed Katan 24a. His colleagues did not grasp his full intent, as with Rabbi Meir, Eruvin 53a. He was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher for eight years; our reading differs (see Rabbi Yochanan). Beitzah 37b: R.A. and R.Y. disagree [ר״א ור״י; referents unresolved]. Ketubbot 111, beginning of b: Rabbah’s brothers sent; Yitzchak, Shimon, and Oshaya said one thing. Yitzchak is Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha; Shimon is Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, some say Resh Lakish; Oshaya is Rabbi Oshaya Berabbi. Maharit asks why Oshaya is listed after Rabbi Yochanan’s student when he was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher. End quotation. Haba Al Yevimto: Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish asked him. Jerusalem Talmud, Ha'arel, halakhah 2, and Asarah Yuchasin, halakhah 6: with Rabbi Yehudah Hanasi and Rabbi Yochanan. His daughter-in-law’s case came before Rabbi Chiyya, who forbade it; Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose said to him, chapter Chalon 80a. Rabbi Oshaya from Rabbi Chiyya (see there). Kirah 38b: “Once we stood above Rabbi Chiyya the elder.”

Since some places spell the name Oshaya with alef and others Hoshaya, in some cases it is uncertain whether Rabbi Oshaya Berabbi above or another Rabbi Oshaya is meant. There are both Rabbi Oshaya and Rav Oshaya. I therefore arranged alphabetically at the end all unqualified Rabbi/Rav Oshaya notices, with their students, teachers, and colleagues. Understand accordingly.
